omar: Quick profiling dump from the nightly perf-run — seeing OOMs on rtx-pool-3 when the prefix store grows > ~8GB during long-chat traces. Repro steps below. TL;DR: shard count + TTL choices are dominating memory footprint and hit-rate tradeoffs, and that interacts badly with workspace sizing in some kernels.

sasha: Can you paste the config you used for the prefix store and the exact repro? Also which model/kernel combo?

omar: Repro is with gptx-7b (fp16 quant path, fused-attn kernels on A100-like instance), load profile: 1200 concurrent short-latency requests (avg seq 512 prefix + 256 generation). Config used:

```
# prefix_store config
shards: 128
ttl_hours: 1
max_memory_mb: 11264  # controller enforced per-gpu
eviction_policy: lru
compression: zstd-1
```

Summary from profiler (30m window):
- shards=128, ttl=1h -> cache_mem ~10.8GB, hitrate=0.72, observed OOMs=6 (all during high concurrent batches)
- shards=32, ttl=4h  -> cache_mem ~6.1GB, hitrate=0.65, observed OOMs=0
- shards=64, ttl=2h  -> cache_mem ~8.2GB, hitrate=0.69, OOMs=1

Observation: fewer shards reduces fragmentation significantly (lower RSS) but slightly reduces hitrate. OOMs correlate more with peak RSS and workspace spike than steady-state cache size.

nicole: Thanks — repro command: `./perf_runner --profile long_chat --concurrency 1200 --model gptx-7b --prefetch true`
I also dumped allocator heap traces and put them in the run artifact: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1772501234/heap.log.gz

Snippet of the producer config we used for the runtime (so you can reproduce allocator behavior):
```
runtime:
  workspace_reserve_mb: 2048
  workspace_growth_policy: conservative
  reuse_buffers: true
kernel_selection:
  prefer_fused_attn: true
  int8_path: enabled
```

james: My two cents: workspace_reserve_mb=2048 is high for many sequences — that reserve is being carved per context in some code paths. Combined with 128 shards of prefix store (which itself allocates per-shard buffers) you end up double-booking memory. We saw a ~18-22% peak mem reduction by:
- lowering workspace_reserve_mb to 768 for int8 paths
- enabling buffer reuse across batch slices (we already have a reuse flag, make sure it's actually hitting fast-path)

Also note some fused kernels still allocate transient scratch for certain sequence lengths; kernel selection should prefer kernels with smaller transient working set for long-prefix tails even if slightly slower.

kevin: Agree with james. Additional thoughts:
- Dynamic shard rebalance: reduce shards when free memory < X and rebuild mapping lazily. This reduces fragmentation and lock contention.
- TTL tradeoff: For our workload, extending TTL from 1h->4h dropped memory but only ~7% hitrate loss; that's acceptable for many customers. We should expose a guided slider in Console ("memory vs hitrate") with recommended presets (low-memory, balanced, aggressive).
- Eviction policy: switch to size-aware LFU for large shards (hot prefixes) to improve effective hit-rate per GB.

infra-bot: [alert] node rtx-pool-3 pod inference-gpu-17 OOMKill at 2026-03-16T14:22:11Z; kernel oom_reaper triggered. Pod restarted (auto-restart).

1) james to run a small matrix this week: workspace_reserve {2048,1024,768} x shards {128,64,32} x ttl {1h,2h,4h} and collect peak RSS + hitrate (owner: james, ETA: 48h)
2) nicole to add a perf test that simulates the repro trace with forced kernel selection that prefers low-scratch kernels (owner: nicole, ETA: EOD tomorrow)
3) kevin to prototype dynamic shard rebalance idea and add a monitoring metric (cache_frag_ratio and hitrate_per_gb) (owner: kevin, ETA: next sprint)
4) infra to add an automated remediation: if free_gpu_mem < 1.5GB and cache_mem > 6GB then drop shard_count by 50% and log an event (owner: infra team, discuss with ops)

sasha: Can we also add a dashboard panel that plots: peak_rss, cache_mem, workspace_reserved, kernel_scratch_allocs over time? That will make regressions much easier to pinpoint.
